title: Google's N-candidate batch discards every paid image when one call refuses or fails
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/providers/google.ts runImage runs N billable calls under Promise.all and asserts each result in a loop; one rejected or `failed`/refused result throws away the images the other calls already returned and the vendor billed.

## Description
runImage (lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:285-331) makes N concurrent calls. `Promise.all` rejects on the first transport failure, and the loop's `assertUsable` throws on the first `status: failed` result, so the 1..N-1 images already returned are dropped. Inside the same function a `completed` result with NO image is tolerated whenever another result carried one (the `!images.length` check at :325 runs only on the total), so the function already accepts a short batch for one failure shape and refuses it for another. For a refusal the router then reroutes, paying a second vendor for N more images. Fixed: Promise.allSettled; return the usable images when at least one arrived, and say on the provenance how many of N were refused/failed (non-silent elimination); throw only when none did.

## Flow
- generate({count: 3}) on google
- call 2 answers status failed with a safety message
- assertUsable throws `refused`; images 1 and 3 discarded
- router books a failed row and reroutes; next vendor makes 3 more

## Expected impact
Frames/extract batches keep the candidates they paid for. Could break: callers that assume images.length === count (grep needed); the provenance needs a field for the short batch.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - paid candidates survive one refusal in a batch
Before: walked: count 3, one refused -> 0 images returned, 2 billed images discarded
After: predicted: 2 images returned, provenance names 1 refused
Method: simulation - a stubbed-fetch probe (imaging-billed-attempts style, count 3, answer 2 refused) decides it; not built because the short-batch provenance field is a contract choice in lib/imaging/types.ts (gateway context)
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: imaging-billed-attempts case: google generate count 3, fetch answers 2nd call {status:'failed', error:{message:'blocked by safety'}}; arm A throws refused with 0 images, arm B returns 2 images and the provenance names the refusal

title: A clip start the vendor received and then timed out on releases its hold unbooked
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/video/leonardo.ts returns `failed` without onAccepted when the v2 start POST throws, so lib/imaging/video/clips.ts releases the hold - even when the request was dispatched (a timeout or a 5xx), which the image chokepoint books as billed.

## Description
errors.ts presumedBilled is 'THE ONE AUTHORITY' on whether a failure cost money: a timeout is billed, a dispatched `failed` is billed. The video start (lib/imaging/video/leonardo.ts:188-214) catches every error into `{kind:'failed'}`; clips.ts run (no `accepted`) calls releaseVideo. A start the vendor accepted but whose answer timed out books $0 in the video-usd window, so the ceiling under-reads exactly in an incident. Fixed: when the caught ImagingError is presumedBilled, settle a failed row at the hold amount (the gate's policy figure), basis estimate.

## Flow
- startClip -> reserve $3.75 (5 s unpriced)
- start POST aborts at 120 s after dispatch
- render returns failed; run() releaseVideo(hold)
- video window: 0 rows, though Leonardo likely charged

## Expected impact
The video ceiling stops under-reading during vendor incidents. Could break: a dispatched-but-unbilled 5xx now consumes window headroom (the same trade the image meter already made).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one billed-attempt rule for image and video
Before: 2 rules: image books dispatched failures, video books none
After: 1 rule (presumedBilled) on both
Method: simulation - walked from clips.ts:216-227 and leonardo.ts:210-214; the video-clips scripted-vendor block can drive it in S (start POST answering an AbortError)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/imaging/video/leonardo.ts:210-214 catch -> {kind:'failed'} (no onAccepted)
lib/imaging/video/clips.ts:216-227 `} else await releaseVideo(hold);`
lib/imaging/errors.ts:157-164 presumedBilled: timeout -> true; failed -> dispatched
instrument: video-clips case: real leonardoVideoAdapter offline, start POST stub rejects with AbortError (dispatched timeout); arm A videoSpendRows() = [], arm B one failed estimate row

title: An empty Ollama recognition is a success; Google's empty recognition is a refusal
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/providers/ollama.ts returns `{text: ""}` as a served recognition when the model answers empty content, while lib/imaging/providers/google.ts raises `refused` for the same shape.

## Description
generative-provider-routing, technique refusal-reroute-hop: 'The safe reading of an empty generation result is refused, never success with zero images'. google.ts:254-255 applies it to recognition; qwen.ts:97-107 treats empty as a soft failure and rotates; ollama.ts:370 trims to "" and returns it (without a schema nothing else catches it). The local eye is first in dev recognize, so an empty local answer reaches the caller as a green, empty judgement. Fixed: empty -> ImagingError `refused` (reroutes to the cloud eye) or `bad-response`. Which kind is a spend question: `refused` reroutes to a billed vendor.

## Flow
- recognize (dev) -> ollama first
- model answers message.content ""
- served with text ""; caller grades nothing

## Expected impact
An empty local read stops passing as a judgement. Could break: a refused kind sends those reads to Google (billed).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the three eyes agree on an empty answer
Before: 3 eyes, 3 behaviours (refused / rotate / success)
After: empty is never a success on any eye
Method: simulation - an imaging-billed-attempts case (withLeaseStore, ollama answers content "") decides arm A vs B; not built because refused-vs-bad-response changes routing spend
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: imaging-billed-attempts case under withLeaseStore: ollama answers {message:{content:''}}; arm A resolves text '', arm B throws (kind per the card's choice); plus a router recognize case asserting the trail

title: Lucid Origin's poll swallows every poll error, like the two adapters fixed this round
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts poll() has the bare `catch { continue; }` that 2a90c1ea and 51e4d526 removed from the video and Flare adapters; a generation whose polls all fail times out naming only the clock.

## Description
poll (lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts poll loop) sleeps a hard-wired 3 s (POLL_INTERVAL_MS) x 60 (MAX_POLLS), with no sleep/limit seam like leonardoFlareProvider's FlareOptions, so the give-up path cannot be driven in a probe without waiting 180 s. Fixed: an options seam (sleep, pollMs, maxPolls) on leonardoProvider, then the same last-poll-error suffix.

## Flow
- start 200
- every poll 401
- after 180 s: 'Leonardo did not finish within 180s.'

## Expected impact
Same as the two built fixes. Could break: router.ts constructs leonardoProvider() bare; an optional argument keeps that call valid.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - 3 of 3 Leonardo pollers keep the last poll error
Before: 1 of 3 still drops it
After: 0 of 3
Method: simulation - the instrument needs a constructor seam first (S), then a case in imaging-billed-attempts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts poll(): `} catch {\n      continue;\n    }`; POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 3_000, MAX_POLLS = 60, no options parameter
instrument: leonardoProvider({sleep, pollMs, maxPolls}) seam, then an imaging-billed-attempts case: every poll 401 -> timeout message carries the 401 sentence

title: The clip store leaves its .tmp behind when the rename never succeeds
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/video/store.ts writeAtomic writes `<file>.<pid>.<n>.tmp` and renames it; when renameRetry exhausts its 20 retries the tmp file stays in foundry-out/clips forever.

## Description
writeAtomic (lib/imaging/video/store.ts:193-198) has no cleanup on a failed rename. An mp4 tmp is up to 200 MB (MAX_CLIP_BYTES). listClipRecords skips non-.json names, so nothing ever reports or removes them. Fixed: on a rename failure, `rm(tmp, {force:true})` then rethrow.

## Flow
- a reader holds the record open past 20 retries (Windows EPERM)
- renameRetry throws
- record/mp4 .tmp left on disk

## Expected impact
Disk under foundry-out/clips stops growing with orphans. Could break: nothing; the tmp is never read.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - 0 orphan tmp files per failed write
Before: 1 orphan per exhausted rename (read from the code)
After: 0
Method: simulation - forcing renameRetry to exhaust needs a seam (RetryOptions are module-private); an S seam or a held-open handle on Windows decides it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: video-clips case: hold the target file open (Windows) or inject a rename that always throws EPERM; assert no *.tmp remains in CLIP_STORE_DIR after writeClipRecord rejects

title: A credit receipt converted to USD is 'estimated' for clips, 'vendor-reported' for images
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/video/pricing.ts labels credits x USD_PER_CREDIT `estimated`; providers/leonardo.ts and providers/leonardoFlare.ts pass the same arithmetic to priceCall as `vendorUsd`, which labels it `vendor-reported`, so the router books it basis `vendor` and the ledger reads it as real money.

## Description
types.ts:132-143 defines `vendor-reported` as a receipt and `estimated` as our arithmetic. video/pricing.ts:338-353 follows that: a credit figure converted at the reference client's 0.00257 is an estimate, only a dollar unit is a receipt. leonardo.ts costUsdFrom and leonardoFlare.ts costOf convert credits at the same rate and hand the product to priceCall's vendorUsd short-circuit (lib/imaging/pricing.ts:252-256), which returns basis vendor-reported; router.ts:417 books that as `vendor`, and lib/ledger costSrcOf maps vendor to 'real'. tests/next-server/imaging-leonardo-flare.test.ts:106 pins the vendor-reported reading for Flare, so the current state is deliberate on one side. Which reading governs - is a credit count from the vendor a receipt once multiplied by our unverified rate? - is the operator's call on what the ledger calls real spend.

## Flow
- Lucid Origin start answers apiCreditCost 10
- costUsdFrom -> 0.0257; priceCall -> vendor-reported
- router books basis vendor; ledger 'real'
- the same 10 credits on a clip book basis estimate; ledger 'model'

## Expected impact
One meaning of CostBasis across the API pool. Could break: whichever side changes moves rows between the ledger's real and model totals.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for a converted credit receipt
Before: 3 converters, 2 rules (1 estimated, 2 vendor-reported)
After: 3 converters, 1 rule
Method: probe - read all three converters and the flare test's pin; the figure is the count, the choice of rule is a direction
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
lib/imaging/video/pricing.ts:331-336 CREDITS -> basis 'estimated'
lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:172 vendorUsd: costUsdFrom(...)
lib/imaging/providers/leonardoFlare.ts:214-217 credits * USD_PER_CREDIT -> priceCall vendorUsd
lib/imaging/pricing.ts:252-256 vendorUsd -> 'vendor-reported'
tests/next-server/imaging-leonardo-flare.test.ts:106 costBasis 'vendor-reported'
